model.backbone: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B diffusion transformer (30 blocks, width 1536) and video VAE, with the LoRA of DVD v1.1 fine-tuned by us
model.depth: D = 1 / max(x + c, tau) with tau = 1e-3; x = the decoded affine-invariant inverse depth in [0, 1] (mean of the three channels of the VAE output), c = the shift of ClipShift; frames are scaled to [-1, 1] before the VAE encoder

clipshift_head.pooling: attention with one learned query, 12 heads

layertap_head.input: final DiT tokens and the outputs of blocks 10 and 20 (block indices 9 and 19), each with a layer normalization and a linear map, summed
layertap_head.output: per frame: translation, rotation quaternion (xyzw), field of view (vertical, horizontal); world-to-camera relative to frame 0
layertap_head.tokens: all tokens of every latent frame (576 at 288 x 512 pixels), with a 2D sinusoidal position embedding

inference.input_size_note: aspect ratio kept, about 288 x 512 pixels, sides multiples of 16, bicubic resize
inference.frames_per_pass: 4k + 1 (the last frame is repeated to reach it)
inference.long_videos: one pass over all frames gives the depth scale; windows give depth and cameras; window depth scaled to the whole-video pass by the median log ratio and blended linearly in log depth over overlaps; cameras chained by the rigid transform averaged over shared frames
inference.intrinsics: all frames share the intrinsic matrix formed from the predicted field of view of frame 0; a longer video takes the median over its windows; principal point at the image center

precision.lora: float32 weights, applied under bfloat16 autocast

inference.time_per_frame_ms: 74 to 84, depth and cameras (Table 2 of the paper)

training.trained_parameters: the LoRA and the two heads (heads in float32)
training.loss: L = L_lat + 0.5 L_grad + L_dec + 4 L_mv + L_cam + L_c + 0.5 L_pts
training.point_loss: valid pixels of a grid of stride 4
training.multi_view_loss: ScanNet++ DSLR and TartanAir clips, frame pairs 1, 2, 4 and 8 apart
training.data: the four image sizes of the benchmarks; clips of 49 frames in a quarter of the steps; 60% of the microbatches from ScanNet, PointOdyssey, Spring, Virtual KITTI 2, Dynamic Replica, DL3DV-10K, the front camera of the Waymo Open Dataset and RealEstate10K, of which DL3DV-10K and Waymo supervise only the cameras and sparse points and RealEstate10K only the cameras
